chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a person has a complaint, let him say: 'In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). I seek Refuge by the Might of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Power of Allah upon whatever He so desires, from the evil of what I find.'

key_terms.اشْتَكَى: to complain or suffer from an ailment

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for seeking relief from illness in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication emphasizes the theological concept of seeking refuge in Allah's absolute power (Qudrah) and might (Izzah) to alleviate physical ailments, reflecting the Shia tradition of combining spiritual reliance with practical healing. The invocation links the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as the intercessor and the embodiment of divine will, reinforcing the connection between prophetic authority and divine cure. This du'a serves as a concise yet comprehensive remedy, addressing both the spiritual and physical dimensions of illness through the remembrance of Allah's name and the Prophet's mission.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu nasr, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When a person has a complaint, so let him say, 
‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I seek Refuge by the Might of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and I seek Refuge with the Power of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to from the evil of what I find’.
en.sarwar: 13. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from al-Thumali from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Whenever one has complains of pain, he should say, ‘In the name of Allah, with (the help of) Allah, and through Muhammad the Messenger of Allah, I seek protection with the majesty of Allah and I seek protection with the power of Allah over everything that He wills, against what I feel.’”
